messages:
Alice: Quick heads-up — I landed an experiment on continuous-batcher heuristics to reduce observed starvation for long sequences when mixed with many short ones. p50 unchanged, p95 down ~6%, p99 up ~12% in the mixed tenant test.
Ben: Can you summarize the heuristic change in one line?
Alice: Switched from strictly size-first batching to token-budget-aware formation with an age boost for older requests. Also added a per-tenant soft window to prevent one tenant from monopolizing the token budget.
Carol: How is the token budget computed?
Alice: It's dynamic: target_batch_tokens = max(base_budget, median_request_len * factor) but capped by per_request_max and global_concurrency. We then bias queue selection by (age_ms * age_weight) to favor waiting long requests.
Dave: Any numbers from profiling?
Alice: Yes — synthetic 50/50 mix (50% short 8t, 50% long 512t) on a 4xA100 node:
- old: throughput 42 req/s, p95 latency 620ms, p99 1180ms
- new: throughput 48 req/s, p95 580ms, p99 1320ms
So overall throughput improved but worst tails for very long requests stepped up, probably due to kernel-switching cost plus larger KV eviction churn.
Erin: Kernel selection might be tripping us. Did you pin execution path for long ones?
Alice: Not yet. We're seeing more kernel reconfigures when a long request enters an in-progress sharded batch of shorts. The runtime currently does lazy kernel selection per-batch based on max sequence length. That causes a recompile/launch penalty occasionally.
Ben: Options: 1) prevent mixing long into an in-flight short-dominated batch (age-priority would then let long wait), 2) preemptively create dedicated long batches when queued long count > threshold, 3) do per-shard kernel warmups.
Carol: I like (2) + (1) fallback. How about a simple policy: if there are >= 3 long reqs in queue OR average queued long_age > 40ms then create long-only batch.
Alice: Implemented that gate in the experiment. The queue policy looks like:
```yaml
queue_policy: dynamic_token_budget
base_budget: 64
factor: 1.3
per_request_max: 1024
long_threshold_count: 3
long_age_ms: 40
age_weight: 0.8
tenant_fair_window_ms: 300
```
Dave: What about KV cache fairness? Long sequences tend to evict useful prefixes for shorts if we don't partition cached slots.
Alice: We added tenant-aware KV cache slices (soft quotas) plus LRU with age bias. Tenants with many long sessions get a capped fraction of KV entries; short-burst tenants keep high-turnover entries. This reduces the cache churn seen in the perf traces.
Erin: Any regressions surfaced by perf-bot?
perf-bot: Regression detected on dataset mixed-prod-v2: p99_tokens_latency +13% (CI: +9%..+17%), RTOs unchanged. See trace: https://perf.internal/runs/1772048
Ben: OK, so p99 increased. Is the p99 dominated by kernel-switch cost or queueing?
Alice: Sampling traces show two classes: (A) long reqs that waited longer then triggered kernel reconfig causing an extra 200-400ms; (B) short requests that were pushed to next batch due to token budget being consumed so they waited ~200ms. Both contribute.
Carol: We should try lowering age_weight slightly and lowering base_budget for short-heavy hosts so shorts get earlier batches. Also, per-tenant burst tokens could save shorts from being starved when a long job arrives.
Alice: Agreed. Next experiment will: reduce age_weight 0.8->0.6, base_budget 64->48 for host profile small-latency, enable preemptive long-only when long_count>=2, and KV soft-slices tuned to 0.2 per active long session.
Dave: Can you paste the A/B commands to toggle?
Alice: Yep — feature flag and config set in runtime:
```
POST /admin/flags
{
  "feature": "dynamic_batcher_v2",
  "enabled": true,
  "params": {
    "age_weight": 0.6,
    "base_budget": 48,
    "long_threshold_count": 2
  }
}
```
Erin: Timeline? If we're careful we can run 4h canary on eu-west then scale. Watch p95/p99 and KV hit-rate.
Alice: I'll start canary at 10:15 UTC and collect traces + KV stats. Will post a short summary here. :rocket: 
perf-bot: Canary started on eu-west; id=canary-1772050
Alice: Canary update after 2h: throughput unchanged, p95 improved 4-7% on small-hosts, p99 back within +3%. KV hit-rate up ~5% for short sessions. Long-session p99 still higher in absolute ms but relative fairness improved.
Ben: Nice. Next follow-ups: add a per-tenant token budget leak-rate to avoid long-term monopolies, and instrument kernel-switch counts per-batch.
Carol: Also add trace tag `batch:mix_type=long_only|short_only|mixed` so we can correlate tail risk.
Alice: Good call — I'll add the tag and push kernel-switch metrics. Will loop back with final canary report and a proposed default config.
Dave: Thanks — this is looking promising.
Alice: Thanks team — I'll post final numbers by EOD.
